title: Physical-Risk-Aware Decentralized Agents for Constrained Vehicle Communications
summary: Decentralized V2X resource control is challenging because each vehicle has only local observations, while reliability depends on network-wide interactions. We develop a physical-risk-aware spatio-temporal graph attention (PA-STGAT) framework for agentic V2X control. Each vehicle perceives its local interaction graph, retains short-term temporal context, and independently selects its PC5 resource and power. Network outcomes are used during centralized training to refine the shared policy. Transmitter-specific credits map reliability failures to individual vehicles. A dual-priced graph term further converts network violations into coordination signals for discrete resource selection, with higher priority on short time-to-collision links. Experiments show higher raw-policy reliability than the tested graph-based baselines. Under filtered execution, PA-STGAT meets the nominal empirical communication requirements across all five seeds, with tradeoffs among utility, delivery reliability, resource occupancy, and filter-induced repair. Compared with GNN+MATD3, it requires fewer resource repairs but achieves lower utility and mean delivery reliability. Mechanism ablations show that removing dual-priced graph coordination causes resource-selection collapse. Density and mobility tests characterize the operating limits of empirical constraint satisfaction.

title: When to Move: Online Repositioning of Movable Antenna Arrays Under a Long-Term Actuation Energy Budget
summary: Movable antenna (MA) arrays improve multiuser throughput by repositioning their elements, but mechanical movement reduces transmission time and consumes actuation energy. Changes in user configurations create nonuniform demand for repositioning over time, while each movement determines which positions are reachable in subsequent slots. Thus, online control must decide when to spend a limited actuation-energy budget, not only where to position the antennas. We formulate causal effective-throughput maximization under displacement-dependent movement delay, inter-slot reachability, and a long-term average actuation-energy constraint. We propose Lyapunov-based online movable-antenna repositioning (LOMA), which adjusts the price of movement through a virtual queue and solves the resulting nonconvex position problem via proximal minorization--maximization, accounting for nonsmooth movement delay and promoting sparse antenna updates. We establish monotone ascent of the smoothed per-slot objective, a finite-horizon sample-path energy bound, almost-sure long-term budget feasibility under a Gaussian fading model with bounded large-scale gains, and a state-matched throughput comparison separating temporal energy allocation from per-slot optimization error. Simulations show that LOMA concentrates actuation after intermittent user changes and improves effective throughput over optimized fixed arrays and a per-slot-budget counterpart, while continuous channel drift favors more frequent incremental repositioning. Additional simulations with pilot-based channel estimates in sparse millimeter-wave channels show that LOMA retains most of the throughput benefits of online repositioning while operating near its prescribed long-term actuation-energy budget.

title: Brain-inspired Beam Selection for mmWave RIS Communication
summary: Beam selection at large passive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) requires either full channel knowledge or beam training, both of which entail unwanted overhead. On the other hand, learned models that predict the optimal codeword from channels sampled at a few active elements avoid both, at the cost of energy-demanding multiply-and-accumulate operations. In this paper, we propose spiking neural network (SNN)-based beam selection for a semi-active RIS assisting a mmWave multiple-input single-output communication system. Direct and sigmoid rate coding are compared against a multi- layer perceptron (MLP) of identical architecture. Energy analysis further reveals that the input layer dominates SNN energy consumption.

title: Efficient Design of Flag Sequence Sets for Delay-Doppler Estimation via Riemannian Optimization
summary: This letter investigates the design of a Flag sequence set with peak-curtain auto-ambiguity functions to enable low-complexity delay-Doppler estimation. Given the predefined Curtain sequences, the Flag sequence set design problem is formulated as the minimization of the weighted integrated masked sidelobe level. To solve this problem, we first reformulate it as an unconstrained optimization problem on the unimodular manifold. Then, a tailored unimodular manifold conjugate gradient (UM-CG) algorithm is developed. Compared with the existing define algorithm, the proposed UM-CG algorithm reduces computational and storage requirements. Moreover, the global convergence of the proposed UM-CG scheme is theoretically derived under mild conditions. Numerical results demonstrate the superior optimization performance of the proposed UM-CG algorithm and show that the designed Flag sequences exhibit nearly ideal peak-curtain properties.

title: Constant-Weight Sparse Vector Coded Augmented-AFDM
summary: Sparse vector coding (SVC) and its variants convey information through sparse vectors (SVs), or sparse support patterns and detecting information by solving sparse recovery problems, making them attractive for short-packet ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC). However, as the required information rate increases, conventional SVC schemes or the enhanced SVC (ESVC) schemes require a rapidly growing number of SVs, resulting in significant increase of complexity and receiver processing latency. On the other hand, when communicating in doubly selective channels, orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) suffers from the Doppler spread induced inter-carrier interference, while affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) experiences the same peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) problem as OFDM, although it allows diversity gain from channel's double selectivity. To address these issues, this paper proposes a constant-weight sparse vector coded augmented AFDM (CW-SVC/A$^2$FDM ) scheme, along with a corresponding joint support and symbol detection algorithm. In this scheme, SVs are represented by constant-weight codewords that feature a fixed Hamming weight and a large Hamming distance, resulting in relatively small SV sets. Simulation results compare various SVC/ESVC schemes and diverse coding schemes employed by the CW-SVC/A$^2$FDM, including Hamming, BCH, RS, and polar codes, for QAM symbol protection. The results demonstrate that the proposed scheme provides a distinct reliability advantage over conventional SVC/ESVC schemes, achieving a gain of up to 14 dB. Furthermore, the study indicates that the CWC's weight and minimum Hamming distance must be carefully selected to balance detection reliability, QAM modulation order, and sparse recovery feasibility, thereby maximizing the overall system's performance.

title: Recursive Semi-Blind Receivers for Wideband Array Processing
summary: Using the commonly employed uniform rectangular array (URA) as an illustrative example, we have recently shown that the block-term tensor decomposition (BTD) model provides a natural representation for the output signal of a multi-dimensional separable sensor array structure in the presence of channel multipath. A palette of effective and efficient semi-blind joint channel estimation/data detection (JCD) algorithms for URA processing, which wed BTD modeling with existing JCD schemes, has thus been developed, and recently extended so as to be applicable in large-scale arrays and/or time-varying environments. However, both the model and the algorithms were based on the assumption of narrowband signals, arriving through paths of effectively the same delay. In this paper, recursive JCD algorithms for wideband sources are developed and evaluated through simulations in a time-varying setting and across different constellation sizes, in comparison with their batch counterparts and the training-only-based solution. They are seen to enjoy the ability to track channel variations and detect the transmitted symbols `on the fly', with the aid of only a short initial training stage.

title: Dynamic Structural Causal Models for Delay Prediction
comment: Accepted in IEEE International Conference on Machine Learning for Communication and Networking (ICMLCN) 2026
summary: Dynamic network key performance indicators (KPIs) such as end-to-end (E2E) delay are shaped by both contemporaneous interactions and temporal persistence. While standard predictors can forecast KPIs under a fixed regime, proactive network management requires reasoning about the effects of explicit actions (interventions) and, in time series, executing a model forward over multiple horizons. We study dynamic structural causal models (DSCMs) for E2E delay in a 5G measurement campaign, where payload and background traffic are intentionally manipulated and thus treated as do-interventions. We learn DSCM scaffolds using four time-series causal discovery methods representing score-based and constraint-based paradigms and common lag-based baselines. Using gradient-boosted decision trees, we evaluate true multi-step DSCM rollout, which recursively simulates the full system state, and a direct target-only ablation that predicts the KPI without recursive simulation. Across two held-out intervention scenarios, including high payload and 10 Mbps background traffic, we find that the inferred target parent/lag sets differ substantially across methods and that rollout behavior is strongly scenario-dependent. In particular, PCMCI+ achieves the best short-horizon rollout accuracy under the payload intervention (RMSE 2.97~ms) but exhibits pronounced horizon-dependent degradation under the background-traffic intervention (root mean squared error (RMSE) ~4.75 ms for long horizon), yielding a large positive rollout tax of up to ~0.78 ms relative to direct prediction; DyNoTEARS and VAR-based DSCMs remain comparatively stable under rollout. These results highlight that evaluating causal scaffolds only via direct prediction can be misleading, and therefore, executability under intervention and long-horizon error propagation are critical for DSCM-based KPI reasoning.

title: Channel Prediction Using Deep Recurrent Neural Network with EVT-based Adaptive Quantile Loss Function
comment: Published in: IEEE Communications Letters ( Volume: 29, Issue: 7, July 2025)
summary: Ultra-reliable low latency communication (URLLC) systems are pivotal for applications demanding high reliability and low latency, such as autonomous vehicles. In such contexts, channel prediction becomes essential to maintaining communication quality, as it allows the system to anticipate and mitigate the effects of fast-fading channels, thereby reducing the risk of packet loss and latency spikes. This letter presents a novel framework that integrates neural networks with extreme value theory (EVT) to enhance channel prediction, focusing on predicting extreme channel events that challenge URLLC performance. We propose an EVT-based adaptive quantile loss function that integrates EVT into the loss function of the deep recurrent neural networks (DRNNs) with gated recurrent units (GRUs) to predict extreme channel conditions efficiently. The numerical results indicate that the proposed GRU model, utilizing the EVT-based adaptive quantile loss function, significantly outperforms the traditional GRU. It predicts a tail portion of 7.26%, which closely aligns with the empirical 7.49%, while the traditional GRU model only predicts 2.4%. This demonstrates the superior capability of the proposed model in capturing tail values that are critical for URLLC systems.

title: Linear Dynamic Range Extension for Rydberg Atomic Receiver via Band-Limited Reconstruction
summary: Rydberg-atom receiver offers a promising approach to radio-frequency (RF) signal reception in wireless communication and sensing systems, combining high sensitivity with the potential for broad frequency coverage. However, the limited linear dynamic range (LDR) of the atomic system causes nonlinear distortion at high input signal levels, thereby restricting the receiver's effective linear input range. To address this issue, we analyze the mechanisms underlying nonlinear distortion in Rydberg atomic receivers and propose a physics-informed band-limited iterative reconstruction (PI-BLIR) method. Specifically, by exploiting the known nonlinear atomic response and signal bandwidth prior, we formulate a constrained maximum-likelihood problem to reconstruct the distorted complex intermediate-frequency (IF) waveform. With the bandwidth constraint absorbed into the frequency-domain parameterization, the constrained maximum-likelihood problem is transformed into an unconstrained optimization problem, which is solved using gradient descent. The proposed method relies solely on digital post-processing and requires no changes to the local-oscillator (LO) field strength, optical parameters, or atomic operating conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that PI-BLIR extends the receiver's LDR by more than 14 dB and enhances the demodulation performance of the atomic receiver.

title: How Robust are Pinching-Antenna Systems to Practical Deployment Imperfections?
summary: This paper investigates the robustness of pinching-antenna systems (PASSs) to three practical deployment imperfections: pinching-antenna (PA) positioning errors, imperfect channel state information (CSI), and line-of-sight (LoS) blockages. We develop analytical frameworks to quantify the performance degradation caused by each imperfection. For PA positioning errors, we employ a Brownian meander model to characterize the distribution and mean of the resulting signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) loss. The results show that positioning errors can diminish the gains from long-term position selection, with the loss becoming more pronounced under stronger shadow fading. For imperfect CSI, we characterize the distribution and moments of the true scattered channel power at the position selected using noisy channel estimates. The resulting selection penalty is governed by the ratio of noise variance to the number of channel measurements, while the upper tail of the selected channel power retains the same behavior as under perfect CSI. Finally, we develop a spatially consistent blockage model and derive the distribution of the optimum long-term SNR for arbitrary blockage configurations, together with a numerically tractable expression for a single blockage. Simulation results validate the analyses and highlight a fundamental property of PASSs: although positioning errors and imperfect CSI can reduce the gains from position selection, good performance can still be achieved provided that an LoS link is available. In particular, even when a large proportion of the waveguide is blocked, PA repositioning can establish LoS links and enable performance close to that of a fully unblocked system for the considered configurations.

title: Physical Prior Mismatch in Variational Dual-Polarization Quantum SATCOM Channel Estimation
summary: Dual-polarization quantum satellite communications require accurate estimation of complex polarization channels. We investigate physical latent-prior mismatch in variational estimation of a $2\times 2$ complex channel, using eight Cartesian latent coordinates and a fixed latent-to-channel mapping. Gaussian, matched and sharpened Rician, Laplace, and Cauchy priors are compared under a fixed neural architecture and forward Kullback-Leibler objective. Models are trained for 300,000 updates with $ζ=1/(2N_{\mathrm{est}})$ and evaluated using three training seeds and 10,000 shared held-out blocks per operating point. The Gaussian and Rician priors coincide at the Rayleigh limit. At higher Rician factors, the matched prior improves estimation accuracy, especially with fewer pilots. At $K=100$ and $N_{\mathrm{est}}=32$, the matched Rician variational estimator reduces mean squared Frobenius error by 2.50% relative to linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE). We also derive a joint Rician Bayesian posterior-mean estimator that incorporates the complete least-squares noise covariance and reduces posterior integration to one-dimensional quadrature. It improves on LMMSE by 3.33% at the same operating point and achieves lower observed error than the scalar Rician and both neural estimators at all 12 operating points. Additional Rician prior sharpening increases error, while Laplace and Cauchy controls remain near the Gaussian baseline.

title: Joint Optimization of Antenna Partitioning and Distortion-Aware Precoding for Massive MIMO-OFDM with Peak Cancellation and In-Band Distortion Compensation
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: In massive MIMO-OFDM systems, peak cancellation (PC) reduces the peak-to-average power ratio but introduces in-band distortion, where compensation signals transmitted from a subset of antennas can suppress this distortion at the users. However, their effectiveness depends on the antenna partition and compensation precoder, while nonlinear power amplifiers (PAs) generate additional distortion. This paper proposes a joint optimization method for antenna partitioning and distortion-aware compensation precoding. To enable this joint optimization, we derive a covariance-based analytical model of PC and PA distortion to predict the per-user, per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plusdistortion- and-noise ratio (SIDNR). The predicted SIDNR is used to select the compensation precoder regularization, the disjoint antenna partition, and the number of compensation antennas. Numerical results demonstrate that joint optimization of the antenna partition and compensation precoder regularization improves BER and SIDNR-based spectral efficiency compared with fixed-partition designs, particularly at high signal-to-noise ratios.

title: BladeSEI: A Multi-Channel and Multi-Day Dataset for Robust Specific Emitter Identification of Radars
summary:
This paper introduces "BladeSEI", a multi-channel receiver, multi-day dataset of radar pulses recorded over-the-air from 12 Software Defined Radios (SDRs) for the purpose of Specific Emitter Identification (SEI). The aim of this dataset is to enable investigation into robust SEI techniques that are able to generalise across different receiver channels and recording sessions.
  The dataset consists of two waveform types per emitter, a 50 microsecond chirped pulse of 40 MHz bandwidth and a 10 microsecond unmodulated pulse. Pulses are captured simultaneously on four synchronised analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) channels of a multi-channel receiver over three recording sessions on two days: a baseline session, an identical repeat on the following day, and a session in which the emitters were thermally conditioned to alter their operating temperature.
  Initial results using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Inception and ResNet based classifiers, trained and tested on a single ADC channel and recording session, show that the BladeRF emitters can be discriminated at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), with ResNet achieving a macro-F1 above 0.98 at 25 dB for both waveforms, and performance degrading towards random guessing at 0 dB.

title: An All-Digital Coherent AFSK Demodulator for CubeSat Applications
comment: Preprint of an article published in Digital Signal Processing (Elsevier), 2025
summary: Audio frequency-shift keying (AFSK) is a widely adopted modulation scheme for CubeSat systems due to its favorable bandwidth efficiency and implementation simplicity. However, coherent detection usually is avoided because synchronization impairments, caused by intense line-of-sight (LOS) dynamics inherent in low Earth orbit (LEO), may significantly degrade the bit error rate (BER). This paper presents a new all-digital coherent AFSK demodulator based on a Kalman filter (KF) for carrier phase and timing delay synchronization and the Viterbi algorithm for bit detection. The Viterbi algorithm is employed for maximum likelihood sequence detection, and the detected bit statistics are fed back to the KF to estimate phase shift, Doppler frequency shift, and Doppler drift induced by the LOS dynamics. Original mathematical analyses are derived to provide a theoretical foundation for the proposed demodulator's operation, specifically addressing its synchronization accuracy in dynamic LEO environments. The proposed demodulator is evaluated considering an additive white Gaussian noise channel with real CubeSat orbits. The performance results obtained through computer simulations demonstrate that the proposed model can withstand such scenarios with a gain of 5 dB in terms of BER compared to the conventional noncoherent AFSK demodulator. The KF performance is assessed using a moving root-mean-square error (MRMSE) statistic and the trace of its state error covariance matrix estimate.
